newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to sell three agro-industry firms.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to sell three agro-industry firms.

text.p: Morocco launched on Friday tenders to sell assets of three small agro-industry companies for a total of 25 million dirhams ($2.8 million) as part of its privatisation programme, a ministry official said.

The firms are Compagnie Maghrebine des Machines Outils a Metaux (C3M), La Societe Nouvelle d'Alimentation et de Fabrication Proteique (SONAFAP) and La Societe Estampage, Matricage et Forgeage (ESMAFOR). They are located respectively in the central city of Fes, the southern region of Agadir and Sale, near Rabat.
The closing date for the tender was set for November 25, 1996 at 1800 GMT, the ministry of privatisation said.

The firms' assets will be sold to individuals or institutions, it said.
The Moroccan government has sold stakes in 46 enterprises since the privatisation programme started in November 1993.
It plans to sell 72 other companies, including banks and two oil refineries, by the end of 1998.
